question: Which British ocean liner was torpedoed by a German submarine off the coast of Ireland in 1915, helping turn American opinion against Germany?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: The sinking killed 128 US citizens and significantly increased American public support for entering the war

extra.why_interesting: Players know a liner was sunk by a U-boat in the First World War but often blur it with Titanic; the stem's date and submarine lock it to one famous name.
extra.verification_notes: Lusitania was torpedoed by U-20 off the Old Head of Kinsale, Ireland, on 7 May 1915, and the sinking turned American opinion against Germany.

explanation: The Lusitania went down in about eighteen minutes, and nearly 1,200 people died, including more than a hundred Americans.

question: In the Pirates of the Caribbean films, what is the name of the ship Captain Jack Sparrow spends the first movie trying to win back?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: Barbossa mutinied against and marooned [him] on a deserted island... Jack is determined to reacquire the Black Pearl

extra.why_interesting: A warm-up everyone can reach; the fun is in remembering that Jack spends most of the first film trying to get the ship back rather than sailing it.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia's plot summary confirms Sparrow spends the first film trying to reacquire the Black Pearl, which Barbossa took in a mutiny.

explanation: The Black Pearl had been stolen by his mutinous first mate Barbossa, which is why Jack starts the film with no ship at all.

question: The cruise ship Costa Concordia capsized in 2012 after striking rocks just off a small island belonging to which country?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: the cruise ship deviated from her planned route at Isola del Giglio, Italy in order to perform a sail-by salute, and as a consequence struck a rock formation

extra.why_interesting: The images of a giant liner lying on its side next to a tiny island were everywhere; the name of the ship itself nudges players toward the right Mediterranean country.
extra.verification_notes: Costa Concordia struck rocks off Isola del Giglio, Italy, on 13 January 2012, per Wikipedia; this is a fixed historical fact.

explanation: She ran aground off Giglio in Tuscany, and the wreck lay on its side in plain view of the island's harbour for more than two years before being refloated.

question: Which English sea captain, denounced as a pirate by Spain, was knighted by Queen Elizabeth the First on the deck of his own ship, the Golden Hind?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: Queen Elizabeth awarded Drake a knighthood aboard Golden Hind in Deptford on 4 April 1581; the dubbing being performed by a French diplomat, Monsieur de Marchaumont.

extra.why_interesting: The man Spain called a pirate was knighted by his own queen on the deck of the very ship he had used to raid Spanish treasure.
extra.verification_notes: Drake was knighted aboard the Golden Hind in 1581 by Elizabeth's award (the physical dubbing was by a French envoy) and Spain branded him a pirate; the answer is unambiguous. Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Francis_Drake

explanation: Drake had just sailed around the world and returned with a hold full of plundered Spanish silver, so the queen came to Deptford in 1581 to reward him in person.

question: When the pirate 'Calico Jack' Rackham was captured in 1720, two members of his crew turned out to be women. Name either of them.
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: Rackham, Bonny, and a crew including another woman, Mary Read, stole the merchant sloop William.

extra.why_interesting: The idea of women fighting on a pirate deck in the 1700s still surprises people, and their story is one of the best documented in the whole era.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Rackham's 1720 capture with two women crew, Anne Bonny and Mary Read, so Anne Bonny is correct.

explanation: Both women escaped hanging by telling the court they were pregnant, and one of them reportedly scolded Rackham that if he had fought like a man he need not have died like a dog.

question: Which ship raced through the night to rescue the roughly 700 survivors sitting in the Titanic's lifeboats?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: rescued over 700 survivors from the ship's lifeboats

extra.why_interesting: Everyone knows the ship that sank; far fewer can name the one that steamed through ice fields all night to pick up the people in the boats.
extra.verification_notes: Carpathia raced through the night and rescued over 700 survivors from Titanic's lifeboats, per Wikipedia.

explanation: The Carpathia's captain, Arthur Rostron, pushed his ship past its normal top speed through the ice to arrive at dawn, and was later honoured in both Britain and America.

question: Gordon Lightfoot's hit 'The Wreck of the Edmund Fitzgerald' tells of a huge freighter lost with all 29 crew in 1975 on which body of water?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: sank in Lake Superior during a storm on November 10, 1975, with the loss of the entire crew of 29 men.

extra.why_interesting: A player assumes a famous shipwreck song is about the ocean; the twist is that a 220-metre freighter vanished with all hands on a lake.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms the Edmund Fitzgerald sank in Lake Superior on Nov 10, 1975 with all 29 crew, matching the question and answer.

explanation: The Fitzgerald was over 220 metres long, yet a November storm on the largest of the Great Lakes sank her so fast that no distress call was ever sent.

question: Tom Hanks played the captain of which container ship, hijacked by Somali pirates in 2009 and later freed by US Navy snipers?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: two US Navy SEAL Team Six snipers of Red Squadron and one USAF CCT from the 24th STS fired shots from Bainbridge's fantail, killing the three remaining pirates.

extra.why_interesting: Players remember the Tom Hanks film but usually only the captain's name; the ship's name is the proud near-miss that reveals who really followed the news story.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Tom Hanks played Capt. Richard Phillips of Maersk Alabama, rescued by Navy SEAL snipers in 2009; later renaming to MV Tygra doesn't change the answer.

explanation: The real Captain Richard Phillips spent five days as a hostage in a lifeboat before SEAL marksmen on a nearby destroyer ended the standoff with three shots.

question: Sweden's great warship Vasa sank on her maiden voyage in 1628 and now fills a museum in Stockholm. Roughly how far did she get from the quay before going down?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: sank after sailing roughly 1,300 m (1,400 yd) into her maiden voyage on 10 August 1628.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume a maiden-voyage disaster means a storm far from port; the truth is the king's pride sailed barely over a kilometre before a gust tipped her over in front of the crowd.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia says Vasa sailed roughly 1,300 m from the quay before sinking, so 'about 1 kilometre' fits; the separate 120 m figure is distance from the nearest shore, not from the quay (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasa_(ship)).

explanation: Vasa was top-heavy and dangerously under-ballasted, so the first strong gust in the harbour rolled her over in sight of the cheering spectators.

question: Alexander Selkirk, the real-life castaway who inspired Robinson Crusoe, spent four years marooned on a Pacific island that today belongs to which South American country?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: Más a Tierra, located in the uninhabited Juan Fernández archipelago 670 km (420 mi) off the coast of Chile.

extra.why_interesting: Readers place Crusoe on a Caribbean island; the real castaway sat on a Pacific island off South America, and a player who knows it is Pacific can reason their way to the country.
extra.verification_notes: Selkirk was marooned on Más a Tierra (now Robinson Crusoe Island) in the Juan Fernández archipelago, which belongs to Chile; the roughly four-year duration matches (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alexander_Selkirk).

explanation: The island lies about 670 kilometres off the Chilean coast, and Chile officially renamed it Robinson Crusoe Island in 1966 to cash in on the connection.

question: Killed in a fight off the coast of North Carolina in 1718, the pirate Edward Teach is far better known by what nickname?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: Edward Teach (or Thatch; c. 1680 – 22 November [3 December N.S.] 1718), better known as Blackbeard, was an English pirate

extra.why_interesting: Players know the nickname instantly but almost nobody knows the ordinary man behind it; the plain surname Teach makes the legend feel suddenly human.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Edward Teach, better known as Blackbeard, was killed at Ocracoke Inlet, North Carolina, in 1718; the spelling variants of his surname don't affect the answer.

explanation: Teach reportedly tied slow-burning fuses into his beard before battle so smoke curled around his face, and his whole piratical career lasted barely two years.

question: Which Swedish warship sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 after sailing little more than a kilometre, and today fills its own museum in Stockholm?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: The ship sank after sailing roughly 1,300 m (1,400 yd) into her maiden voyage on 10 August 1628.

extra.why_interesting: A flagship built to dominate the Baltic never left its own harbour; the player expects a wreck story at sea and gets one that ends within sight of the shipyard.
extra.verification_notes: Vasa sank on its maiden voyage on 10 August 1628 after about 1,300 m and is housed in the Vasa Museum in Stockholm (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vasa_(ship)).

explanation: A gust tipped the top-heavy ship over in front of the crowds, and after more than three centuries in the cold, low-salt water it was lifted almost intact in 1961.

question: Found drifting in the Atlantic in 1872, seaworthy and with its cargo of alcohol still aboard but not a soul on deck, which ship became the world's most famous ghost ship?
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: dishevelled but seaworthy condition under partial sail

extra.why_interesting: The player assumes a 'ghost ship' is folklore; this one was a real, documented vessel whose crew simply vanished with the ship still perfectly sailable.
extra.verification_notes: Mary Celeste was found adrift 4 Dec 1872, seaworthy with 1,701 barrels of alcohol aboard and crew missing; no later developments change this (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mary_Celeste).

explanation: The crew's single lifeboat was missing and the ship's papers were gone, yet the vessel sailed on for about ten days with nobody at the wheel, and no trace of the people was ever found.

question: True or false: in the early 1800s, a pirate fleet of tens of thousands of men on the coast of China was commanded by a woman.
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: the fleet consisted of approximately 400 junks and between 40,000 and 70,000 pirates.

extra.why_interesting: Players picture pirate chiefs as Caribbean men like Blackbeard; the largest pirate force in history was Chinese and commanded by a woman, who also negotiated an amnesty and died in peace.
extra.verification_notes: Zheng Yi Sao led the Red Flag Fleet, a confederation of tens of thousands of pirates, off the coast of China from 1807 to 1810 (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Zheng_Yi_Sao).

explanation: Zheng Yi Sao took over her late husband's Red Flag Fleet and led it against the Qing navy, then negotiated a pardon that let her retire and die peacefully in her sixties.

question: Robert Ballard's famous 1985 expedition that found the Titanic was officially a cover story. What had the US Navy really sent him to inspect on the Atlantic floor?
alternative_answers: the wrecks of Thresher and Scorpion
topic: Shipwrecks, pirates and the high seas
source_excerpt: The Navy directed Ballard to find two nuclear-powered attack submarines that had sunk in the 1960s: the USS Scorpion and the USS Thresher.

extra.why_interesting: Players assume finding the Titanic was the whole point of the famous 1985 expedition. In fact it was the side project: the US Navy only paid for it so Ballard could secretly check on two lost Cold War nuclear subs, and the Titanic hunt got the leftover days.
extra.verification_notes: Navy's real mission was surveying the wrecks of nuclear subs USS Thresher and USS Scorpion, per the Washington Times report on Ballard's 2008 disclosure; no newer events change this.

explanation: The Navy wanted the wrecks of the lost subs USS Thresher and USS Scorpion checked for radiation leaks and clues to their sinking, and only after that job was done did Ballard get about twelve days to hunt for the Titanic.
